source.title: Is This the Subspace You Are Looking for? An Interpretability Illusion for Subspace Activation Patching
source.authors: Aleksandar Makelov; Georg Lange; Atticus Geiger; Neel Nanda

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study uses subspace activation patching and linear-subspace representations as interpretability tools, but it does not test whether sparse features are superposed, whether capacity pressure explains polysemanticity, or whether SAE features are canonical units.
record.gate_note: The paper cites superposition and polysemanticity as context and discusses the linear representation hypothesis, but its experiments concern whether subspace activation patching faithfully localizes task-relevant information. Those results do not test the versions of the claim. The rows below record related results about subspace patching as findings that fit no version. Cited results from other work and values used only to train or select directions are excluded.
record.test_reason: The paper studies whether subspace activation patching (DAS) faithfully localizes a task variable in GPT2-Small and GPT2-XL. It invokes superposition and polysemanticity only as motivation for the linear representation hypothesis. It measures no feature sparsity, capacity competition, neuron polysemanticity, SAE features, or feature dimensionality. Its results bear on interpretability-method faithfulness, not on any version of the claim.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that subspace activation patching can give illusory interpretations by activating dormant parallel pathways, shown in IOI (MLP8) and in factual recall. They link this to rank-1 (ROME) editing working regardless of where a fact is stored. They also show a faithful residual-stream direction, and recommend patching in bottlenecks such as the residual stream plus validation beyond end-to-end effects.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies subspace activation patching and DAS, not the toy-model method or measurements of superposition in the cited original source.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes differ by intervention location (MLP versus residual stream), by whether the direction's causally disconnected component is retained, and by subspace dimension (1-dimensional versus 100-dimensional, with decomposed 200-dimensional tests).

fits_no_version.finding: A 1-D DAS direction in GPT2-Small MLP8 gives 46.7% FLDD, but drops to 13.5% once its Wout-nullspace component is removed. Full-MLP patching gives -8%. A 100-D MLP subspace shows the same pattern (62% falls to 17%). Residual-stream directions keep their effect without the proxy nullspace component (140.7% vs 127.5%). Factual-recall DAS patches in GPT2-XL show the same illusion.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Subspace activation patching can attribute a feature to a subspace that merely activates a dormant pathway through a causally disconnected component, so patch success alone does not show the subspace represents the feature.

record.problems: The experiments do not measure superposition, feature sparsity, capacity competition, or SAE feature completeness. The principal IOI experiment uses GPT2-Small; the reported subspace-patching outcomes are task-specific, and the paper notes that only a limited set of real-world settings are studied.
record.rows_left_out: Factual-recall and ROME comparisons were left out because they evaluate fact-editing interventions rather than the claim versions about superposition, polysemanticity, or feature-unit geometry. The paper's cited findings from other work were also excluded.

untested.parts: All: no toy model with sparse features. The paper's toy linear network is about patching illusions, not superposition.
All: capacity competition and dedicated dimensions for important features are not examined.
All: the origins of polysemantic neurons are not examined.
All: no measure of features spread across neurons and no dictionary or SAE recovery.
All: no SAE features are trained or evaluated.
All: 1-D vs 100-D DAS subspaces are compared only for patching strength, not for the dimensionality of the model's feature units.

record.verdict_notes: The only mentions of superposition and polysemanticity are motivating citations to Elhage et al. 2022. Appendix E results (MLP weights are full-rank; linear separability survives GELU) concern patching mechanics, not superposition. No verdicts are given because no version is tested.

versions.untested_parts: Sparse-feature superposition, feature sparsity, feature importance, transition behavior, and regular geometry.
Whether capacity pressure causes polysemanticity or whether important features get dedicated dimensions.
Whether polysemanticity arises through mechanisms other than capacity pressure.
Whether LLM features are spread across neurons or recoverable with a dictionary or SAE.
Whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
The dimensionality of actual superposed features; the paper compares patching subspaces of different dimensions, not the dimensionality of the model's true feature units.
